integration_notes: Match occupation using the retained O*NET-SOC Code; do not use this occupation code alone to infer backend specialization, entry-level seniority, or posting geography.
Software Skills Workplace Example names are technology examples; their Element ID and Element Name are source categories, not unique technology identifiers.
Essential Skills and Transferable Skills have element-level ratings. Retain their source element IDs, source category names, scale IDs, ranges, and names separately from posting mention frequency.
Content Model Reference provides the actual element names and hierarchy. Period-separated parent prefixes are documented in its official data dictionary.
The source Software Skills Hot Technology and In Demand flags are retained as source metadata; they are not mention rates in the Kaggle snapshot.
All CSV cells were read as strings to preserve identifiers. Numeric ratings were converted only in the joined inspection summary.
No canonical skill aliases, job posting filters, or source-specific production ingestion were implemented in this inspection.
limitations: This is a selected seven-file O*NET download, not the entire database.
O*NET describes occupations broadly; these associations do not establish entry-level backend requirements.
No source collection dates are asserted; some Software Developers rows have source update month 08/2025 within release 31.0.
The selected O*NET release must remain pinned when reproducing these joins. A later release can change file structures and associations.
O*NET data alone cannot establish available job-posting sample size or snapshot mention frequencies.
